name: Kelly

scaling.scaled: 20" box (step-ups allowed), 14/10 lb ball, 3-4 rounds. This is a 25-35 minute workout even scaled — start slower than feels right.
scaling.beginner: 3 rounds: 200m run, 15 box step-ups, 15 light wall-balls. Volume is the hazard here, not load — cut rounds before cutting movements.

origin.summary: Five rounds of a 400m run, thirty box jumps, and thirty wall-balls — one of the longer Girls, a half-hour grind for most athletes. Nothing is heavy; the test is staying in continuous motion when every movement taxes the legs the previous one just used. Part of CrossFit's original 'Girls' benchmark series — named workouts introduced by founder Greg Glassman starting in 2003, on the logic that anything that leaves you flat on your back deserves a name like a storm. They serve as repeatable fitness tests: revisit one every few months and the clock tells you whether you're fitter. First posted to CrossFit.com on 2005-04-10.

description: Five rounds of a 400m run, box jumps, and wall-ball shots — a running-anchored triplet pairing two lower-body-dominant movements with the run.
source_notes: crossfit.com/faq/wod (official CrossFit FAQ, 'Explain The Workouts with Names (the Girls)?'), retrieved 2026-07-08
